amount.label: Monthly Treasury Statement, table 5, net outlays by agency, fiscal year to date at 30 September
amount.note: These are Treasury's own closed accounts, not a forecast. Refresh once the fiscal year ends in September. The figures come from the API at api.fiscaldata.treasury.gov, dataset mts_table_5, filtered to record_date 2025-09-30, taking the Total-- rows at nesting level 2.

totalOutlays.label: Final Monthly Treasury Statement, FY2025, total outlays
totalOutlays.note: The Total Outlays line in the same table. Every slice below must add up to it.

note.label: The cost case on each slice: what the money buys now against what it bought before
note.note: A slice that only names the job argues the other side's case, so every note carries a published cost trend as well as the Treasury amount. Each claim names its own publisher in the slice's source list. Re-sample when a publisher issues a new edition, not on the calendar.

categories.name: Health: Medicare, Medicaid and the rest
categories.agency: Department of Health and Human Services
categories.note: The largest single line in the budget, and it did not make care cheaper. On HHS's own figures the average individual premium went from $2,784 in 2013 to $5,712 in 2017, a rise of 105%. Health now takes 18.0% of the whole economy.

source.label: Final Monthly Treasury Statement, FY2025, table 5
HHS ASPE, Individual Market Premium Changes 2013-2017
CMS, National Health Expenditures 2024 Highlights

categories.name: Social Security
categories.note: Paid out as it comes in. There is no account with your name on it. The trustees put the 75-year shortfall at $25.1 trillion, and the fund empties in 2034.

source.label: Final Monthly Treasury Statement, FY2025, table 5
2025 OASDI Trustees Report, highlights

categories.name: The Treasury, most of it interest on the debt
categories.note: Gross interest on the debt alone was $1,215.6 billion of this. Net of the trust funds, CBO puts it near $970 billion. Either figure beats the whole military slice below, and it buys nothing at all.

source.label: Final Monthly Treasury Statement, FY2025, table 5

categories.name: The military
categories.note: Military programs only. Veterans, nuclear weapons and the spy agencies are counted elsewhere. Nobody can audit it and nobody can hold its price: GAO found $49.3 billion of weapon-program cost growth in a single year.

source.label: Final Monthly Treasury Statement, FY2025, table 5
GAO-25-107569, Weapon Systems Annual Assessment 2025

categories.name: Veterans
categories.note: The bill for the wars, paid decades after the fighting stops. CBO measured VA spending rising from $64 billion in 2000 to $180 billion in 2017, after inflation. Its share of the budget nearly doubled in seventeen years.

source.label: Final Monthly Treasury Statement, FY2025, table 5
CBO, Possible Higher Spending Paths for Veterans' Benefits

categories.name: Food and farm programs
categories.note: Food assistance and farm support, in one department. USDA grades its own accuracy: the SNAP error rate was 10.93% in 2024, about $10.5 billion paid wrong. No grocer stays open at that rate.

source.label: Final Monthly Treasury Statement, FY2025, table 5
USDA FNS, FY2024 SNAP Quality Control payment error rates

categories.name: Federal employee pensions
categories.note: Retirement and health benefits for people who worked for the government. CBO priced them against comparable private-sector work: 43% dearer, and 93% dearer at high-school level. You pay the difference on a package you cannot buy yourself.

source.label: Final Monthly Treasury Statement, FY2025, table 5
CBO, Comparing the Compensation of Federal and Private-Sector Employees in 2022

categories.name: Roads, rail and air
categories.note: Everything people picture when they say roads and bridges. Under two cents of the dollar, and the dearest building in the world: New York lays subway at about $1.5 billion a kilometer, against a global median near $220 million.

source.label: Final Monthly Treasury Statement, FY2025, table 5
NYU Marron Institute, Transit Costs Project data

categories.name: Homeland Security
categories.note: Borders, customs, the coast guard, airport screening and disaster relief. The department is 23 years old and has already doubled in real terms, from $55.9 billion to $115.3 billion in the same dollars. It grew faster than the budget around it.

source.label: Final Monthly Treasury Statement, FY2025, table 5
USAFacts, Department of Homeland Security spending

categories.name: Everything else, after receipts
categories.agency: Twenty remaining agencies, less undistributed offsetting receipts
categories.note: Energy, housing, labor, justice, the environment, education, the State Department, NASA, the courts and Congress together spent $514.5 billion. The government nets $337.8 billion of its own receipts against that, leaving this. Take the schools out of it: real spending per pupil has more than doubled since 1970, and 17-year-olds score no better than they did then.

source.label: Final Monthly Treasury Statement, FY2025, table 5
NCES Fast Facts, long-term trends in reading and mathematics achievement
NCES Fast Facts, expenditures per pupil
